chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I attend the mosques with my neighbor and others, so they instruct me to lead the prayer with them. I have already prayed before I went to them, and sometimes the weak and the ignorant pray behind me, following my prayer. I dislike advancing [to lead] when I have prayed in the state of those I have specified to you who follow my prayer. So order me regarding this with your command, to which I will adhere and act upon, God willing.' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Pray with them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I have already prayed individually but am asked to lead the congregation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Hasan (AS) addresses the practical dilemma of a worshipper who has already prayed individually but is requested to lead the congregation, ruling that he should accept the role of Imam. This establishes the principle that prior individual prayer does not invalidate one's eligibility to lead, thereby encouraging communal unity and preventing the neglect of congregational prayers due to minor technical concerns. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on facilitating social cohesion in worship over rigid exclusivity.
